name: Silver Pink
lede: Silver Pink is a greyed-out pink first filed by the ISCC-NBS system in 1955, so close to [[black-shadows]] on screen that the two are nearly indistinguishable, with a darker variant of its own called Dark Silver Pink.

sections.title: A grey pink with a dark child
sections.body:
The 1955 ISCC-NBS circular places Silver Pink in its grayish pink block, less than 1 color-unit from that block's own center, among the tightest fits in the system [1]. The Munsell notation is 3.8R 7.2/2.2 [1]. Our library carries several older names it has been sold or printed under, including Cloud Pink, Pinkish Grey and Light Heliotrope-Grey, though none of our sources dates them [1].

Silver Pink has one documented child in the library, Dark Silver Pink, a deeper version of the same grey-pink [1]. It shares its family word, "silver," with [[silver-fern]] and [[silver-green]] from this same batch, though the three are not otherwise linked [1]. On screen, Black Shadows sits only 2.7 units away, described here as almost the same [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
Our archive finds this grey pink in 0.53 percent of 23,781 paintings, 127 of them, and the within-painting lens isolates it as a dominant area in 74, as photographed [2]. That ranks it ahead of 55 percent of the named colors we track [2]. It peaks in the 1900s, in 22 of 1,674 paintings, present in 1.3 percent of the 1,674 paintings (22 of them) dated to that century, 3.0 times its museums' baseline rate [2].

Inside a painting it most often plays a light, 61 percent of its 74 appearances by lightness rank [2]. The earliest match in our archive is a 1452 panel by Bartolomeo Caporali, 503 years before the ISCC-NBS system's 1955 record of the name; that gap marks a look-alike hue in an aged photograph, not the pigment itself, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [2]. It is also over-represented in French painting, 2.3 times the expected rate, 27 of 3,443 French works in the archive [2].
